decisions.statement: An act here names no change and runs no change.
An act reaches the edits kept beside the calling agent's page.
How one edit is said in a report is worded here rather than by each act.
One reading of the lines piped in serves every act that names paths.
An act words its own refusals rather than borrowing another act's words.
An act naming paths reads each path against the repository root.
An act naming paths leaves every edit no path named.
An act piping nothing in is refused rather than reaching every edit.
A path naming no edit an act reaches refuses that act rather than being passed over.
A drop reaches the edits kept.
An act saying `all: true` reaches every edit that act reaches.
`all` takes `true` and no other value.
An act names each edit that went.
An act naming paths says how many edits are still there.
An edit a move left behind is reached by the path that move came from.
A drop saying `all: true` over no edit kept says so rather than refusing.
A drop saying `all: true` takes every edit away though a row reads as no edit.
That drop says a row read as no edit rather than naming each edit that went.
A drop naming paths over a row that reads as no edit is refused as before.
A listing of the edits kept names each edit and the call landing those edits.
The refusal an agent whose page is nowhere reads is worded here for every call over the edits kept.
That refusal opens by naming the retry, which costs only the wait.
That refusal says nothing was kept, so a retry loses nothing.
That refusal names the log to read next before it explains anything.
That refusal says how long the wait for the queued cause has run to.
That refusal names all three causes rather than the one that clears.
That refusal names this repository's history as what says whether the page was written.
That refusal says the log carries a line only where a landing refused.
That refusal says a log naming the page nowhere is no sign that no landing ran.
A landing refused for any reason but the lock or a put-back is retried by nothing.
A landing that ended before it could say why is retried by nothing.
That refusal says it read the index and no file on disk, and asserts no reason none is named.
That refusal tells the agent to say it is refused to whoever dispatched it.
That refusal promises no outcome from waiting.
That refusal names no act the agent reading it is refused.
A call naming no agent at all is refused without the retry.
A refusal composed where no index answers is said without the retry.
A subagent dispatched or resumed a moment ago can run before that page lands.
Every answer here is built by a function rather than written out as a value.
A turn over the edits kept that would not open is an operational fault.
Nothing here reads an argument off the command line.
Nothing here lands.
An edit kept that no longer fits its body refuses by that edit rather than by the page.
That refusal names which edit of how many kept went stale.
That refusal says the path it names is the stale edit's rather than the call's.
That refusal says the edits kept beside it are held back rather than at fault.
That refusal names the drop over that one path rather than over every edit kept.
An edit kept that went stale is a fault of the data rather than an operational one.
A throw that no edit kept accounts for is said as it was thrown.

definition: the acts run over the edits kept rather than over a change
